history.sg_progress: In accordance with General Assembly resolution 77/304, a scalability model report will be submitted to the Assembly during its seventy-ninth session. The Administration will take advantage of that report to undertake a comprehensive analysis of interconnected issues linked to the support account and the support entities, including the relative balance of work funded by the support account and the regular budget, including the backstopping of special political missions. Even as some peace operations close, the Secretariat is facing increasing demand to support others that are deploying, which has implications for the support account. The Administration needs to retain the capacity to deploy peace operations as mandated. These requirements need to be integrated into the development of a consolidated scalability model. The model should acknowledge that many services of the entities funded by the support account also support special political missions and other United Nations clients, in accordance with their mandated functions. It should also reflect the management paradigm shift approved by the General Assembly whereby the new Headquarters departments – the Department of Operational Support and the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance – have provided operational and policy support to all Secretariat entities from 2019. The model therefore needs to consider the entire spectrum of support provided to United Nations peace and security functions, which will require adequate funding for the support provided to entities other than peacekeeping operations.

history.sg_progress: In accordance with General Assembly resolution 77/304 on the support account for peacekeeping operations, a report on the scalability of the support account will be submitted to the Assembly at its seventy-ninth session. The report provides a comprehensive analysis of interconnected issues linked to the support account, including the relative balance of work funded by the support account and the regular budget, including to the backstopping of special political missions. As part of the project, led by the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance, regarding the support account and related funding issues, an external consultancy has been working with the United Nations Logistics Base and the Regional Service Centre on scalability. The findings from that review will inform future budget proposals for the United Nations Logistics Base and the Regional Service Centre, with the results expected to be included in the budget proposal for the 2026/27 period.

history.administration_response: The Administration requests the closure of this recommendation because it was implemented. The report of the Secretary-General on the support account and related funding issues (A/79/781) was submitted to the General Assembly in its second resumed session. The Assembly took note of the report in its resolution 79/298. As regards the service centres, the independent consultant has completed the review, and a scalability model will be applied in future budgets.
history.board_assessment: The scalability model for the support account has been deployed. Therefore, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
